newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Ecuador welcomes WTO banana ruling, EU declines comment.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador welcomes WTO banana ruling, EU declines comment.

text.p: Ecuador, the world's biggest banana exporter, welcomed a ruling by a World Trade Organisation (WTO) panel on Tuesday that the European Union's banana regime violates world trade rules.
"The current EU banana regime discriminates against banana imports from Ecuador," Ecuador's ambassador to the EU, Alfredo Pinoargote, said in a statement.
Bananas represent one-third of Ecuador's total exports and as a developing country it depended on fair access to the EU market, he added.

Under EU banana import rules introduced in 1993, EU and mainly Caribbean countries are allocated 30 percent of banana import licences to the detriment of Ecuadorian producers and EU consumers, the statement said.
Latin American bananas are cheaper than those produced by African, Caribbean and Pacific (ACP) countries which enjoy preferential access to the EU market under the terms of the Lome convention.
"It is iniquitous that Ecuadorian producers must purchase these licences in order to maintain their historic access to the EU market," Pinoargote said, adding that this had cost millions of dollars.
A European Commission spokesman said he had no immediate comment on the WTO ruling.
"It's a very detailed and complex report which we shall have to study carefully," agriculture spokesman Gerard Kiely said.
